topics.title: Space
topics.description: Blast off and learn about planets, stars, and the moon!
funFacts: The Sun is a star, and it's so big that about 1 million Earths could fit inside it.
A day on Venus is longer than a year on Venus.
Saturn's rings are made mostly of ice and rock.
Astronauts float in space because there's very little gravity to pull them down.

questions.question: Which planet is known as the Red Planet?
questions.explanation: Mars looks red because its surface is covered in iron oxide (rust).

questions.question: What is at the center of our solar system?
questions.explanation: The Sun is a star at the center of our solar system, and all planets orbit around it.

questions.question: What do we call a large rock that orbits the Sun, smaller than a planet?
questions.explanation: Asteroids are rocky objects that orbit the Sun, mostly found in the asteroid belt.

questions.question: Which planet has the famous rings we can see from Earth?
questions.explanation: Saturn's rings are made of ice and rock and are visible even with a small telescope.

questions.question: What is the name of Earth's natural satellite?
questions.explanation: The Moon orbits the Earth and is the only natural satellite Earth has.

questions.question: Which planet is closest to the Sun?
questions.explanation: Mercury is the closest planet to the Sun and also the smallest planet.

questions.question: Which is the largest planet in our solar system?
questions.explanation: Jupiter is by far the largest planet — you could fit over 1,000 Earths inside it.

questions.question: Which planet is the hottest, even though it's not closest to the Sun?
questions.explanation: Venus has thick clouds that trap heat, making it hotter than Mercury.

questions.question: Which planet is the farthest from the Sun?
questions.explanation: Neptune is the farthest official planet from the Sun.

questions.question: What is the name of the galaxy we live in?
questions.explanation: Our solar system is part of the Milky Way galaxy.

questions.question: What do astronauts wear to survive in space?
questions.explanation: Spacesuits protect astronauts and supply the oxygen they need to breathe.

questions.question: What force keeps the planets orbiting the Sun?
questions.explanation: Gravity from the Sun pulls on the planets and keeps them in orbit.

questions.question: What tool do scientists use to see faraway stars and planets?
questions.explanation: Telescopes make faraway objects in space appear closer and clearer.

questions.question: What do we call a group of stars that forms a picture in the sky?
questions.explanation: A constellation is a pattern of stars, like the Big Dipper or Orion.

questions.question: What is a 'shooting star' actually?
options: A meteor burning up in the sky
questions.explanation: A shooting star is a small piece of rock or dust burning up as it enters Earth's atmosphere.

questions.question: What is a comet mostly made of?
questions.explanation: Comets are often called 'dirty snowballs' because they're made of ice, dust, and rock.

questions.question: How many moons does Mars have?
questions.explanation: Mars has two small moons, named Phobos and Deimos.

questions.question: What do we call one full spin of the Earth on its axis?
questions.explanation: One full rotation of Earth takes about 24 hours, which we call a day.

questions.question: What do we call one full trip Earth makes around the Sun?
questions.explanation: It takes Earth about 365 days to orbit the Sun once — that's one year.

questions.question: What do we call a piece of space rock that survives falling to Earth's surface?
questions.explanation: If a meteor doesn't burn up completely and lands on Earth, it's called a meteorite.

questions.question: What is Pluto now classified as?
questions.explanation: In 2006, scientists reclassified Pluto as a dwarf planet instead of a full planet.

questions.question: What causes day and night on Earth?
options: Earth moving closer to the Sun
questions.explanation: As Earth rotates, different parts face toward or away from the Sun, causing day and night.

questions.question: What do we call the path a planet takes as it travels around the Sun?
questions.explanation: An orbit is the curved path an object follows around another object in space.

questions.question: What is the closest star to Earth?
questions.explanation: The Sun is a star, and it's by far the closest one to Earth.

questions.question: What kind of vehicle carries astronauts into space?
questions.explanation: Rockets are powerful enough to escape Earth's gravity and carry astronauts into space.

topics.title: Animals
topics.description: Discover amazing facts about animals big and small.
funFacts: A group of lions is called a pride.
Octopuses have three hearts.
Bats are the only mammals that can truly fly.
A snail can sleep for three years.

questions.question: Which animal is known as the 'King of the Jungle'?
questions.explanation: The lion is often called the King of the Jungle, even though it mostly lives in grasslands.

questions.question: How many hearts does an octopus have?
questions.explanation: Octopuses have three hearts — two pump blood to the gills, one pumps it to the body.

questions.question: Which of these animals can truly fly?
questions.explanation: Bats are mammals, but unlike most mammals, they can truly fly.

questions.question: What do we call baby frogs?
questions.explanation: Baby frogs are called tadpoles and live in water before growing legs.

questions.question: Which animal is the tallest in the world?
questions.explanation: Giraffes can grow up to 18 feet tall, making them the tallest land animal.

questions.question: Which animal is the fastest on land?
questions.explanation: Cheetahs can run up to 70 miles per hour, making them the fastest land animal.

questions.question: Which is the largest animal on Earth?
questions.explanation: The blue whale is the largest animal to have ever lived, even bigger than the biggest dinosaurs.

questions.question: Which animal can change color to blend in with its surroundings?
questions.explanation: Chameleons change color to hide from predators, show emotion, and control their temperature.

questions.question: Which animal carries its baby in a pouch?
questions.explanation: Kangaroos are marsupials and carry their babies, called joeys, in a pouch.

questions.question: Which animal sleeps through most of the winter?
questions.explanation: Many bears hibernate through winter, slowing their body down to save energy.

questions.question: Which insect makes honey?
questions.explanation: Bees collect nectar from flowers and turn it into honey.

questions.question: Which animal has black and white stripes?
questions.explanation: Every zebra has a unique stripe pattern, just like human fingerprints.

questions.question: Which bird cannot fly and lives in cold places like Antarctica?
questions.explanation: Penguins can't fly, but they're excellent swimmers.

questions.question: Which animal can regrow its tail if it loses it?
questions.explanation: Many lizards can drop their tail to escape a predator and then grow a new one.

questions.question: Which animal is often called 'man's best friend'?
questions.explanation: Dogs have lived alongside humans for thousands of years as loyal companions.

questions.question: What do we call a group of lions?
questions.explanation: A group of lions living together is called a pride.

questions.question: What do we call a group of wolves?
questions.explanation: Wolves live and hunt together in groups called packs.

questions.question: Which animal has the longest neck?
questions.explanation: A giraffe's long neck helps it reach leaves high up in trees.

questions.question: What do spiders spin to catch their prey?
questions.explanation: Spiders spin sticky silk webs to trap insects for food.

questions.question: Which sea animal has eight arms?
questions.explanation: An octopus has eight flexible arms covered in suckers.

questions.question: Which animal is known for its long trunk?
questions.explanation: An elephant uses its trunk to breathe, smell, drink, and grab things.

questions.question: What do we call animals that eat only plants?
questions.explanation: Herbivores, like rabbits and cows, eat only plants.

questions.question: What do we call animals that eat only meat?
questions.explanation: Carnivores, like lions and wolves, mainly eat other animals.

questions.question: What do we call animals that eat both plants and meat?
questions.explanation: Omnivores, like bears and humans, eat both plants and meat.

questions.question: Which insect changes from a caterpillar into a flying insect?
questions.explanation: A caterpillar forms a chrysalis and transforms into a butterfly through metamorphosis.

topics.title: Human Body
topics.description: Explore how your amazing body works.
funFacts: Your heart beats about 100,000 times a day.
Bones make up about 15% of your body weight.
Your skin is the largest organ in your body.
You blink around 15-20 times every minute.

questions.question: Which organ pumps blood through your body?
questions.explanation: The heart pumps blood through blood vessels to every part of your body.

questions.question: What is the largest organ in the human body?
questions.explanation: Your skin covers your whole body and is actually your largest organ.

questions.question: Which part of your body helps you breathe?
questions.explanation: Your lungs take in oxygen from the air and remove carbon dioxide from your body.

questions.question: How many bones does an adult human body have?
questions.explanation: Adults have 206 bones, though babies are born with more that fuse together over time.

questions.question: What do your eyes need to help you see?
questions.explanation: Eyes need light to see; light bounces off objects and enters your eyes.

questions.question: What hard part of your body protects your brain?
questions.explanation: The skull is a hard bony case that protects your brain from injury.

questions.question: What carries messages between your brain and the rest of your body?
questions.explanation: Nerves send electrical signals between your brain and body super fast.

questions.question: Which organs filter waste out of your blood?
questions.explanation: Kidneys filter waste and extra water out of your blood to make urine.

questions.question: Which organ helps break down the food you eat?
questions.explanation: Your stomach uses acid and muscle movement to break down food.

questions.question: What do teeth mainly help you do?
questions.explanation: Teeth break food into smaller pieces so it's easier to swallow and digest.

questions.question: Which muscle in your body never stops working, even while you sleep?
questions.explanation: Your heart is a muscle that beats constantly to keep blood flowing.

questions.question: How many main senses do humans usually have?
questions.explanation: The five main senses are sight, hearing, smell, taste, and touch.

questions.question: Which body part is mainly used for the sense of smell?
questions.explanation: Your nose detects smells in the air around you.

questions.question: Which body part is mainly used for the sense of taste?
questions.explanation: Taste buds on your tongue help you sense flavors like sweet and salty.

questions.question: Which body part is mainly used for the sense of hearing?
questions.explanation: Your ears pick up sound waves and send signals to your brain.

questions.question: Which body part is mainly used for the sense of touch?
questions.explanation: Skin is covered in tiny nerve endings that let you feel textures, heat, and pressure.

questions.question: Which body part is mainly used for the sense of sight?
questions.explanation: Your eyes detect light and send images to your brain to help you see.

questions.question: What is the red liquid your heart pumps around your body?
questions.explanation: Blood carries oxygen and nutrients to every part of your body.

questions.question: What do we call breathing in oxygen and breathing out carbon dioxide?
questions.explanation: Respiration is the process of breathing that exchanges oxygen and carbon dioxide.

questions.question: Which organ do you use to think, learn, and remember?
questions.explanation: Your brain controls thinking, memory, and everything your body does.

questions.question: What connects your muscles to your bones?
questions.explanation: Tendons are tough cords that attach muscles to bones so you can move.

questions.question: What connects one bone to another bone?
questions.explanation: Ligaments are strong bands that hold bones together at joints.

questions.question: What is the hard, white outer layer of your teeth called?
questions.explanation: Enamel is the hardest substance in your body and protects your teeth.

questions.question: How many chambers does the human heart have?
questions.explanation: The heart has four chambers that work together to pump blood.

questions.question: What do we call the process of food being broken down and used by your body?
questions.explanation: Digestion breaks food down into nutrients your body can use for energy.

topics.title: Plants
topics.description: Learn how plants grow and make their own food.
funFacts: Plants make their own food using sunlight in a process called photosynthesis.
Some trees can live for thousands of years.
Bamboo is one of the fastest-growing plants on Earth.
Not all plants need soil to grow — some grow in water!

questions.question: What do plants use sunlight, water, and air to make?
questions.explanation: Through photosynthesis, plants turn sunlight, water, and carbon dioxide into food (sugar) and oxygen.

questions.question: Which part of the plant absorbs water from the soil?
questions.explanation: Roots grow underground and absorb water and nutrients from the soil.

questions.question: What gas do plants release that humans and animals need to breathe?
questions.explanation: Plants release oxygen as a byproduct of photosynthesis, which we need to breathe.

questions.question: What is the name for a young plant that has just sprouted from a seed?
questions.explanation: A seedling is a young plant that has just grown from a seed.

questions.question: Which part of the plant usually attracts bees for pollination?
questions.explanation: Flowers often have bright colors and scents that attract bees and other pollinators.

questions.question: What is the green substance in leaves that helps plants make food?
questions.explanation: Chlorophyll gives plants their green color and helps capture sunlight for photosynthesis.

questions.question: Which part of the plant carries water from the roots up to the leaves?
questions.explanation: The stem acts like a pipe, moving water and nutrients from the roots to the rest of the plant.

questions.question: Which of these is NOT something a plant needs to grow?
questions.explanation: Plants need sunlight, water, and nutrients to grow — not electronics!

questions.question: In which season do most plants begin to bloom in many places?
questions.explanation: Spring's warmer weather and rain help many plants start growing and blooming.

questions.question: What do we call the process of a seed starting to grow?
questions.explanation: Germination is when a seed begins to sprout and grow into a plant.

questions.question: Where are a plant's seeds usually found?
questions.explanation: Many plants grow fruit around their seeds to help protect and spread them.

questions.question: Besides water and carbon dioxide, what else do plants need for photosynthesis?
questions.explanation: Sunlight provides the energy plants need to turn water and carbon dioxide into food.

questions.question: Which gas do plants take in from the air during photosynthesis?
questions.explanation: Plants absorb carbon dioxide from the air to help make their food.

questions.question: What is the tough outer layer of a tree's trunk called?
questions.explanation: Bark protects the tree trunk from damage, insects, and disease.

questions.question: What do we call plants that live and grow for many years?
questions.explanation: Perennial plants, like many trees, live for more than two years.

questions.question: What do we call plants that complete their life cycle in just one year?
questions.explanation: Annual plants grow, flower, produce seeds, and die all within one year.

questions.question: A cactus is specially adapted to live in which environment?
questions.explanation: Cacti store water in their thick stems, helping them survive in dry deserts.

questions.question: What do we call the practice of growing crops and raising plants for food?
questions.explanation: Agriculture is the science and practice of farming plants and animals.

questions.question: What often helps carry pollen from one flower to another?
questions.explanation: Bees, butterflies, and even wind help move pollen so plants can reproduce.

questions.question: What do we call trees that keep their leaves green all year round?
questions.explanation: Evergreen trees, like pine trees, don't lose all their leaves in the fall.

questions.question: What do we call trees that lose their leaves in the fall?
questions.explanation: Deciduous trees, like oak and maple, drop their leaves each autumn.

questions.question: What part of the plant usually grows underground?
questions.explanation: Roots grow underground to anchor the plant and absorb water and nutrients.

questions.question: Which of these plants grows extremely fast and is actually a type of grass?
questions.explanation: Bamboo is a giant grass and one of the fastest-growing plants in the world.

questions.question: What do we call the colorful part of a plant that often smells nice?
questions.explanation: Flowers are often colorful and fragrant to attract pollinators like bees.

questions.question: What sticky sweet liquid do flowers produce to attract insects?
questions.explanation: Nectar is a sweet liquid flowers make to attract bees and other pollinators.

topics.title: Weather
topics.description: Find out what causes rain, wind, snow, and storms.
funFacts: Lightning is hotter than the surface of the Sun.
No two snowflakes are exactly alike.
A rainbow is caused by sunlight passing through raindrops.
Hurricanes are called typhoons in the Pacific Ocean.

questions.question: What causes rain to fall from clouds?
questions.explanation: When water droplets in a cloud combine and become too heavy to stay in the air, they fall as rain.

questions.question: What is frozen rain called?
questions.explanation: Hail forms when raindrops freeze into ice inside very cold storm clouds.

questions.question: What instrument measures temperature?
questions.explanation: A thermometer measures how hot or cold something is.

questions.question: What causes a rainbow to appear?
questions.explanation: Rainbows form when sunlight passes through raindrops and bends into different colors.

questions.question: What do we call a very strong spinning column of air that touches the ground?
questions.explanation: A tornado is a fast-spinning column of air that reaches from a storm cloud down to the ground.

questions.question: What instrument measures how fast the wind is blowing?
questions.explanation: An anemometer has spinning cups that measure wind speed.

questions.question: What instrument measures air pressure?
questions.explanation: A barometer measures air pressure, which helps predict changing weather.

questions.question: What do we call frozen precipitation that falls in soft, white flakes?
questions.explanation: Snow forms when water vapor freezes into ice crystals high in the clouds.

questions.question: What is fog?
options: A cloud that touches the ground
questions.explanation: Fog is basically a cloud that forms very close to or on the ground.

questions.question: Which season is usually the hottest in many places?
questions.explanation: Summer has the most direct sunlight and longest days, making it the hottest season.

questions.question: Which season is usually the coldest in many places?
questions.explanation: Winter has the least direct sunlight and shortest days, making it the coldest season.

questions.question: What causes the loud sound of thunder?
options: Air heating up rapidly from lightning
questions.explanation: Lightning heats the air so quickly that it expands and creates the sound we hear as thunder.

questions.question: What is lightning?
options: A flash of electricity in the sky
questions.explanation: Lightning is a giant spark of electricity that happens during a thunderstorm.

questions.question: What do we call a very powerful tropical storm with strong winds and heavy rain?
questions.explanation: Hurricanes are huge spinning storms that form over warm ocean water.

questions.question: What do we call the amount of water vapor in the air?
questions.explanation: Humidity describes how much moisture is in the air.

questions.question: Which type of cloud looks big, white, and fluffy like cotton?
questions.explanation: Cumulus clouds are the puffy, cotton-like clouds you often see on sunny days.

questions.question: Which type of cloud is thin, high, and wispy?
questions.explanation: Cirrus clouds are thin, feathery clouds high in the sky, often seen in fair weather.

questions.question: What do we call a long period of time with little or no rain?
questions.explanation: A drought happens when an area doesn't get enough rain for a long time.

questions.question: What do we call the constant movement of water between the sky and Earth?
questions.explanation: The water cycle describes how water evaporates, forms clouds, and falls back as rain or snow.

questions.question: What happens to water when it evaporates?
questions.explanation: Evaporation turns liquid water into water vapor, which rises into the air.

questions.question: What happens to water vapor when it cools inside a cloud?
questions.explanation: Condensation happens when water vapor cools and turns back into liquid droplets, forming clouds.

questions.question: What do we call the four main periods of weather patterns during the year?
questions.explanation: The four seasons — spring, summer, autumn, and winter — each have typical weather patterns.

questions.question: What do we call scientists who study and predict the weather?
questions.explanation: Meteorologists study the atmosphere to forecast the weather.

questions.question: At what temperature does water freeze, in Celsius?
questions.explanation: Water freezes into ice at 0 degrees Celsius (32°F).

questions.question: At what temperature does water boil, in Celsius?
questions.explanation: Water boils and turns to steam at 100 degrees Celsius (212°F) at sea level.

topics.title: Simple Machines
topics.description: See how levers, wheels, and ramps make work easier.
funFacts: A seesaw is an example of a lever.
Wheels reduce friction, making it easier to move things.
A ramp is also called an inclined plane.
Scissors use two levers working together.

questions.question: Which simple machine is a seesaw an example of?
questions.explanation: A seesaw is a lever that pivots on a fixed point called a fulcrum.

questions.question: What simple machine helps you lift a flag up a flagpole?
questions.explanation: A pulley uses a wheel and rope to make lifting things easier.

questions.question: What do we call a flat surface set at an angle, like a slide?
questions.explanation: An inclined plane (or ramp) makes it easier to move objects to a higher or lower place.

questions.question: Which simple machine is used in a doorknob?
questions.explanation: A doorknob works as a wheel and axle, turning a small motion into a larger one.

questions.question: What simple machine is a knife or axe blade an example of?
questions.explanation: A wedge is a tool with a thin edge used to cut or split things apart.

questions.question: Which simple machine is basically an inclined plane wrapped around a pole?
questions.explanation: A screw is like a ramp wound around a cylinder, used to hold things together or lift materials.

questions.question: What do we call the fixed point that a lever pivots or balances on?
questions.explanation: The fulcrum is the point a lever rests on and turns around.

questions.question: Which simple machine is commonly used in a bolt or screw-top jar lid?
questions.explanation: Screws use spiral grooves to hold materials together tightly.

questions.question: What do wheels help reduce, making it easier to move heavy objects?
questions.explanation: Wheels reduce friction between an object and the ground, making it easier to push or pull.

questions.question: A skateboard ramp is an example of which simple machine?
questions.explanation: A ramp is an inclined plane that helps change the height of movement smoothly.

questions.question: Which two simple machines work together to make a pair of scissors?
questions.explanation: Scissors are made of two levers joined at a pivot point (like a fulcrum) with wedge-shaped blades.

questions.question: Which simple machine helps a wheelbarrow lift heavy loads more easily?
options: Wheel and axle combined with a lever
questions.explanation: A wheelbarrow uses a wheel and axle along with lever action from the handles.

questions.question: What do we call simple tools that make work easier by changing the force needed?
questions.explanation: Simple machines are basic tools that help us do work with less effort.

questions.question: A crowbar used to pry something open is an example of which simple machine?
questions.explanation: A crowbar is a lever that multiplies the force you apply to pry or lift things.

questions.question: A winding, zigzag mountain road is an example of which simple machine idea?
questions.explanation: Zigzag roads use gentler inclined planes to make climbing steep mountains easier.

questions.question: What do simple machines generally make it easier for us to do?
questions.explanation: Simple machines help us move, lift, or hold objects using less effort.

questions.question: A pulley on a flagpole is mainly used for what task?
questions.explanation: A pulley system lets you pull down on a rope to raise the flag upward.

questions.question: Which of these is NOT a simple machine?
questions.explanation: A battery stores electricity — it isn't one of the six classic simple machines.

questions.question: Besides lever, wedge, pulley, wheel and axle, and inclined plane, what is the sixth type of simple machine?
questions.explanation: The screw is the sixth simple machine, essentially an inclined plane wrapped around a cylinder.

questions.question: A ramp leading into the back of a moving truck is an example of which simple machine?
questions.explanation: The ramp is an inclined plane, making it easier to roll heavy items up into the truck.

questions.question: An axe used to split wood is an example of which simple machine?
questions.explanation: The axe's blade is a wedge, forcing wood apart as it's driven in.

questions.question: What do we call a machine made of two or more simple machines working together?
questions.explanation: A compound machine, like a bicycle or a can opener, combines several simple machines.

questions.question: A bottle opener that pops off a cap works using which simple machine?
questions.explanation: A bottle opener acts as a lever, using a small pivot point to pry the cap off.

questions.question: A spiral staircase is similar in shape to which simple machine?
questions.explanation: A spiral staircase winds upward like the threads of a screw.

questions.question: A see-saw at a playground works using which simple machine?
questions.explanation: A see-saw is a classic example of a lever balancing on a central fulcrum.
